title: Apple Stock Drops Amid More Worry Over iPhone Sales - Barron's
text:
Apple Stock Drops Amid More Signs of Low Demand for Newest iPhones By Updated Dec. 6, 2018 12:14 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Text size
Reviewers told smartphone buyers to hold off on Apple ’s (AAPL) two new high-end phones to wait for the (somewhat) less-expensive XR . Customers don’t appear to have listened.
A survey of 6,900 consumers, reported Thursday by UBS, said global intentions to buy new iPhones are down from last year’s levels. New models, which in recent years have made up as much as three quarters of the units sold, now represent less than 60% of consumers’ intended purchases.
“This is largely related to particularly weak XR demand—a notion matched by ongoing downward XR revisions in the supply chain,” analyst Timothy Arcuri wrote Thursday.
UBS, which has a Buy rating on Apple stock, dropped its price target on the shares to $210, below FactSet’s average, from $225. The shares were down nearly 3% to around $171 late Thursday morning as global equities fell . Newsletter Sign-up
Analysts have lately expressed more bearishness about iPhone sales growth. Earlier this week, Tae Kim covered a downgrade at HSBC Global Research, where analyst Erwan Rambourg said ”Apple’s iconic hardware unit growth is broadly over for now.” (He also covered downbeat guidance from Cirrus Logic (CRUS), a major Apple chip supplier .)
The conversation around slowing iPhone sales, however, has been going on for some time—which Arcuri acknowledged. “Weak iPhone demand is hardly a revelation and the narrative is clearly going to keep shifting to services,” he wrote.
UBS expects iPhone revenue to drop 2% year-over-year in fiscal 2019, with rising average selling prices unable to completely offset a decline in unit sales. FactSet’s consensus projects roughly flat revenues. Recommended Reading
